fact: SMEX reports that Libya's National Charter for AI Ethics (adopted 1 June 2026) proposes a national oversight body for AI ethics, to be created by the Council of Ministers, to supervise compliance, approve high-risk systems and keep a registry of compliance certifications.
The Journal of the Academic Forum article abstract says a legislative vacuum in Libya leaves AI-related crimes, including deepfakes, unaddressed, and that Libyan legislation must be updated.

Libya's National Council for Public Freedoms and Human Rights says its draft personal data protection law, referred to the House of Representatives as an initial proposal, includes a chapter on artificial intelligence covering personal data in training and running AI systems, privacy, transparency, accountability and limiting discrimination.
